title: Arab Federation
capsule: The Arab Federation (الاتحاد العربي الهاشمي) was a short-lived constitutional union between the Hashimite kingdoms of Iraq and Jordan, formed on February 14, 1958 in direct response to the rival United Arab Republic proclaimed by Egypt and Syria ten days earlier. King Faisal II of Iraq served as federal head of state and his uncle Crown Prince Abd al-Ilah as federal prime minister, while Jordan's King Hussein retained internal authority over Amman. The federation lasted barely five months: the Iraqi monarchy was abolished in the 14 July 1958 coup by Abd al-Karim Qasim, which killed Faisal II and Abd al-Ilah, and Jordan formally withdrew from the federation on August 2, 1958.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The federation comprised the well-defined national territories of Iraq and Jordan; its territorial extent is unambiguous, though it possessed no new jointly administered regions distinct from its constituent kingdoms.
